segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Kathryn and today we're going to be helping you find someone to help out around the house.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Kathryn，今天我们将帮助您在房子周围找人帮忙。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we're looking for someone to help us do some things around the house.
segments.zh: 所以我们正在找人来帮助我们在房子周围做一些事情。

segments.en: So we're going to talk about this more in depth.
segments.zh: 所以我们将更深入地讨论这个问题。

segments.en: But first, let's take a look at one word on vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 但首先，让我们看一下关于词汇预览的一个词。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: So the beginning of today's dialogue has to do with a newspaper ad.
segments.zh: 所以今天对话的开始与报纸广告有关。

segments.en: We are writing an ad for the newspaper.
segments.zh: 我们正在为报纸写广告。

segments.en: Now what exactly is a newspaper ad, Marco?
segments.zh: 现在什么是报纸广告，马可？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in the newspapers, usually there is a section called the classifieds where people post ads or advertisements or adverts where maybe they're selling their car or they're looking to hire people.
segments.zh: 因此，在报纸上，通常有一个名为 Classifieds 的部分，人们发布广告、广告或广告，他们可能正在出售他们的汽车或他们正在寻找雇用人员。

segments.en: So this is what a newspaper ad is.
segments.zh: 所以这就是报纸广告。

segments.en: You're selling something, you're buying something or maybe you want to hire people, etc.
segments.zh: 你在卖东西，你在买东西，或者你想雇人，等等。

segments.en: It is basically an advertisement in the newspaper to find help.
segments.zh: 它基本上是报纸上寻求帮助的广告。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's listen to our dialogue and when we come back, we'll be talking more about the words and phrases you've heard.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听我们的对话，当我们回来时，我们会更多地谈论你听到的单词和短语。

segments.en: Can you help me write a newspaper ad?
segments.zh: 能帮我写一则报纸广告吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: What are you looking to buy or sell?
segments.zh: 你是想买什么，还是卖什么？

segments.en: Actually, I want to hire someone to help me around the house.
segments.zh: 其实，我想雇个人帮我做家务。

segments.en: Oh, you want to get a maid?
segments.zh: 哦，你想请个女佣？

segments.en: Well, I think it's better if you call her a cleaning lady or domestic help.
segments.zh: 我觉得叫清洁阿姨或家政人员更合适。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what do you want her to do?
segments.zh: 那你想让她做些什么？

segments.en: Well, let's see.
segments.zh: 嗯，我们来看看。

segments.en: I want her to come in three times a week for a couple of hours to clean the kitchen, bathroom and maybe do some cooking.
segments.zh: 我想让她每周来三次，每次干几小时，打扫厨房和浴室，也许再做点饭。

segments.en: Got it.
segments.zh: 明白了。

segments.en: And how much do you offer per month?
segments.zh: 你准备每月付多少？

segments.en: I would pay her hourly.
segments.zh: 我打算按小时付钱。

segments.en: I don't know what the going rate is though.
segments.zh: 不过我不知道现在的行情价是多少。

segments.en: I know for sure it's more than minimum wage, but maybe you should just negotiate with the person that answers the ad.
segments.zh: 时薪肯定高于最低工资，不过你最好跟应聘的人当面谈谈价。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: Thanks for your help.
segments.zh: 谢谢你帮忙！

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at language takeaway.
segments.zh: 现在来看看“语言要点”。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So first of all today, Marco, the advertisement is about wanting to hire someone.
segments.zh: 所以首先，马可，广告是关于想雇用某人的。

segments.en: Now, this is an important verb, especially when we're trying to find help.
segments.zh: 现在，这是一个重要的动词，尤其是当我们试图寻求帮助时。

segments.en: The verb to hire.
segments.zh: 雇用的动词。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So to hire means to give someone work, to offer a contract to someone.
segments.zh: 所以雇佣意味着给某人工作，向某人提供合同。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So my boss hired me three years ago.
segments.zh: 所以我的老板三年前雇用了我。

segments.en: That means he gave me a job three years ago.
segments.zh: 这意味着他三年前给了我一份工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But this is not just for office jobs.
segments.zh: 但这不仅仅是办公室工作。

segments.en: This is for all kinds of jobs.
segments.zh: 这适用于各种工作。

segments.en: So what about cutting your grass or doing your lawn?
segments.zh: 那么割草或做草坪呢？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you can hire a gardener, for example, and it's basically the same thing.
segments.zh: 例如，您可以聘请园丁，这基本上是一样的。

segments.en: It means that you're going to pay someone to work for you.
segments.zh: 这意味着你要花钱请人为你工作。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's say you wanted to hire a maid, M-A-I-D, a maid.
segments.zh: 所以假设你想雇一个女仆，m-a-i-d，一个女仆。

segments.en: But this is a little bit old fashioned, this word.
segments.zh: 但这有点过时，这个词。

segments.en: What does a maid do or what did a maid do?
segments.zh: 女仆做什么或女仆做什么？

segments.en: Well, a maid is basically a woman, a female servant, so to say, a person that basically serves you.
segments.zh: 好吧，女仆基本上是一个女人，一个女仆，可以这么说，一个基本上为你服务的人。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So she cleans the house.
segments.zh: 所以她打扫房子。

segments.en: She maybe puts the covers on the beds, washes the dishes, cooks, does all of these domestic things.
segments.zh: 她可能把被子放在床上，洗碗，厨师，做所有这些家务。

segments.en: So she works around the house.
segments.zh: 所以她在房子周围工作。

segments.en: But because there's a bad association, we don't like to think, oh, we have servants.
segments.zh: 但是因为有不好的联想，我们不喜欢想，哦，我们有仆人。

segments.en: We don't say maid anymore.
segments.zh: 我们不再说女仆了。

segments.en: We have two other ways of saying this word.
segments.zh: 我们还有两种表达这个词的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we could say that we want to hire a cleaning lady, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们可以说我们想聘请清洁女工，对吧？

segments.en: Or we want to hire domestic help.
segments.zh: 或者我们想聘请家庭帮助。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now there's an important difference between these two words.
segments.zh: 现在这两个词之间有一个重要的区别。

segments.en: First of all, cleaning lady is a woman, a lady, and she is someone who only cleans.
segments.zh: 首先，清洁女是个女人，一个女人，她是一个只打扫卫生的人。

segments.en: She doesn't take care of your children.
segments.zh: 她不照顾你的孩子。

segments.en: She doesn't walk your dogs.
segments.zh: 她不遛你的狗。

segments.en: She basically just cleans the house, washes the dishes, cleans the clothes, washes the floors.
segments.zh: 她基本上只是打扫房子，洗碗，洗衣服，洗地板。

segments.en: So she's a cleaning lady.
segments.zh: 所以她是个清洁工。

segments.en: Now domestic help, this is a little bit more general.
segments.zh: 现在家庭帮手，这一点一般。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So domestic help would be a little bit more in depth of what the person's going to do.
segments.zh: 因此，家庭帮助会更深入地了解该人将要做的事情。

segments.en: So we'll help with the domestic work, with domestic meaning the house.
segments.zh: 所以我们将帮助家庭工作，以及家庭意义。

segments.en: So this person will maybe cook for you, clean the house, take care of the kids, do everything that is associated with the house.
segments.zh: 所以这个人可能会为你做饭，打扫房子，照顾孩子，做与房子相关的一切。

segments.en: So it's important to see that domestic means something that has to do with the house.
segments.zh: 因此，重要的是要看到国内意味着与房子有关的东西。

segments.en: This is help man or woman in the house.
segments.zh: 这是家里的帮助男人或女人。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's all we have for language takeaway, but we do have another section, Fluency Builder, in which we're going to look at some great words and phrases.
segments.zh: 所以这就是我们为语言外卖所拥有的一切，但我们确实有另一个部分，Flueny Builder，我们将在其中查看一些很棒的单词和短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So first on Fluency Builder, let's take a look at how we're going to pay the person because obviously we were saying that we want to hire this person.
segments.zh: 所以首先在 Fluency Builder 上，让我们来看看我们将如何向这个人付款，因为显然我们是在说我们想雇用这个人。

segments.en: We're going to pay them.
segments.zh: 我们要付钱给他们。

segments.en: So how are we going to pay them?
segments.zh: 那么我们将如何付款呢？

segments.en: The person said, I would pay the woman her hourly.
segments.zh: 那个人说，我会每小时付钱给她。

segments.en: I would pay her hourly.
segments.zh: 我打算按小时付钱。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is the rate.
segments.zh: 所以这是费率。

segments.en: This is how much she will be paid.
segments.zh: 这就是她将获得多少报酬。

segments.en: And we don't say she will be paid $10,000 per year.
segments.zh: 我们并不是说她每年会得到 10,000 美元的报酬。

segments.en: We say she'll be paid $10 per hour.
segments.zh: 我们说她每小时会得到 10 美元的报酬。

segments.en: So we pay per hour.
segments.zh: 所以我们每小时付费。

segments.en: This is paying her hourly.
segments.zh: 这是每小时付钱给她。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if you have an hourly wage, that means that you get paid per hour.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您有时薪，这意味着您每小时获得报酬。

segments.en: In contrast with a salary, that means that you would get a fixed amount every month.
segments.zh: 与薪水相反，这意味着您每个月都会获得固定金额。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So if the monthly salary is $1,000, for example, you could break that down and say, but every day you earn 100.
segments.zh: 例如，如果月薪是 1,000 美元，你可以把它分解并说，但你每天都能赚到 100。

segments.en: You work 10 days.
segments.zh: 你工作10天。

segments.en: But if it's hourly, you say you'll get paid $10 per hour.
segments.zh: 但如果是每小时，你说你会得到每小时 10 美元的报酬。

segments.en: So if you work four hours today, you will earn $40.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您今天工作四个小时，您将获得 40 美元。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So now we want to pay the cleaning lady hourly, but we don't know what the going rate is.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们想每小时付钱给清洁工，但我们不知道现在的价格是多少。

segments.en: Going rate.
segments.zh: 去率。

segments.en: Going.
segments.zh: 去。

segments.en: So this is an interesting phrase and it's important to notice that it's not going rate is an amount of money, but it's not always the same.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的短语，重要的是要注意它的价格不是一定的数量，但并不总是一样的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It depends on the industry.
segments.zh: 这取决于行业。

segments.en: So the going rate for a teacher is different from the going rate for a cleaning lady, which is different from the going rate for a language tutor.
segments.zh: 因此，教师的现行率与清洁女工的现行率不同，这与语言导师的现行率不同。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or like an English tutor.
segments.zh: 或者像英国导师一样。

segments.en: So first of all, the going rate is how much these people, these cleaning ladies normally earn.
segments.zh: 所以首先，这些人的现行率是这些人，这些清洁工通常的收入。

segments.en: It's an average.
segments.zh: 这是一个平均值。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you would usually calculate it, say the approximate going rate is between maybe $8 to $10 per hour.
segments.zh: 所以你通常会计算它，假设大约每小时 8 到 10 美元之间。

segments.en: So it's not like an exact amount.
segments.zh: 所以它不像一个确切的数量。

segments.en: You would say the going rate is more or less a certain amount.
segments.zh: 你会说现在的利率或多或少是一定的数量。

segments.en: It's not exact.
segments.zh: 这并不准确。

segments.en: So you might ask your friends, what do you pay your cleaning lady?
segments.zh: 所以你可能会问你的朋友，你付给你的清洁工付什么钱？

segments.en: And one friend says, oh, I pay $12 per hour.
segments.zh: 一位朋友说，哦，我每小时支付 12 美元。

segments.en: And my other friend says, oh, I pay about $8 per hour.
segments.zh: 我的另一个朋友说，哦，我每小时支付大约 8 美元。

segments.en: So to me, it sounds like the going rate is about $10 per hour.
segments.zh: 所以对我来说，这听起来像是每小时 10 美元左右。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So we're not really sure what the going rate is.
segments.zh: 所以我们不确定现在的价格是多少。

segments.en: So our friend says, well, you know what?
segments.zh: 所以我们的朋友说，好吧，你知道吗？

segments.en: I'm sure it's more than minimum wage.
segments.zh: 我敢肯定，这不仅仅是最低工资。

segments.en: Now minimum wage is actually something that the government decides on or either the federal government in America or the state.
segments.zh: 现在，最低工资实际上是政府决定的，或者是美国或州的联邦政府。

segments.en: And each state will have a number that they say that is the least you can pay a person per hour.
segments.zh: 每个州都有一个他们说的数字，这是您每小时最多可以支付一个人的费用。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it is the law.
segments.zh: 所以这是法律。

segments.en: If you pay less, it's illegal.
segments.zh: 如果你少付钱，那是非法的。

segments.en: And this is because we expect everyone to be treated fairly.
segments.zh: 这是因为我们希望每个人都得到公平对待。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's not an advantage of people.
segments.zh: 所以这不是人的优势。

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: And so, for example, in America, in my state, Illinois, I think the minimum wage is $7.25 per hour.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，在美国，在我所在的伊利诺伊州，我认为最低工资是每小时 7.25 美元。

segments.en: Oh, really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: It's pretty high.
segments.zh: 它相当高。

segments.en: And this is because people need to pay for health care and cars and houses and children.
segments.zh: 这是因为人们需要支付医疗保健、汽车、房屋和儿童的费用。

segments.en: So we say the least you can pay someone is $7.25.
segments.zh: 所以我们说你至少可以付钱给某人是 7.25 美元。

segments.en: Now this is different.
segments.zh: 现在这是不同的。

segments.en: As you said, it could be different from state to state.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，它可能因州而异。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Because I know in some states, if I'm not mistaken, it's like $5.50 or something.
segments.zh: 因为我知道在某些州，如果我没记错的话，这就像 5.50 美元之类的。

segments.en: Yeah, some states it's $5.
segments.zh: 是的，有些州是 5 美元。

segments.en: It depends on the cost of living.
segments.zh: 这取决于生活成本。

segments.en: If it's cheap to rent an apartment or to find transportation, then obviously the minimum wage is going to be lower.
segments.zh: 如果租公寓或寻找交通工具很便宜，那么显然最低工资会更低。

segments.en: Obviously there's no maximum wage.
segments.zh: 显然没有最高工资。

segments.en: There's no number that is the most you can pay someone.
segments.zh: 没有一个数字是您可以支付给某人的最多的。

segments.en: But all states have a minimum wage.
segments.zh: 但所有州都有最低工资。

segments.en: It's the least that you can pay someone per hour.
segments.zh: 这是您每小时可以支付某人的最少费用。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So for our last phrase, we don't know what the minimum wage is, we're not really sure what the going rate is.
segments.zh: 所以对于我们的最后一句话，我们不知道最低工资是多少，我们不确定现行率是多少。

segments.en: So we should just negotiate with the person that answers the ad.
segments.zh: 所以我们应该与回答广告的人进行谈判。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now to negotiate is a great verb.
segments.zh: 现在谈判是一个很好的动词。

segments.en: It is something that all of us do all the time.
segments.zh: 这是我们所有人一直在做的事情。

segments.en: So to negotiate means to try and compromise or to reach an agreement.
segments.zh: 所以谈判意味着尝试和妥协或达成协议。

segments.en: So maybe I say the most I will pay is $11.
segments.zh: 所以也许我说我支付的最多是 11 美元。

segments.en: So I say, okay, I'll pay you $9.
segments.zh: 所以我说，好吧，我会付给你 9 美元。

segments.en: And I say, no, I'll take 12.
segments.zh: 我说，不，我要12。

segments.en: Yeah, sorry, 12 is too much.
segments.zh: 是的，对不起，12太过分了。

segments.en: I'll pay you 10.
segments.zh: 我给你10。

segments.en: Okay, 11.
Okay, agreed.
segments.zh: 好的，同意。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's a way of reaching an agreement, like you say, where both sides have their goals and they try to find a price that is the best for both parties.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种达成协议的方式，就像你说的，双方都有自己的目标，他们试图找到对双方最好的价格。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's basically a verb to negotiate and this is what you do, as you said, in many circumstances, especially when you're getting a job.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上是一个动词，这就是你所做的，正如你所说，在许多情况下，尤其是当你找到工作时。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's listen to the dialogue one last time and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 所以让我们最后一次听对话，我们会回来一会儿。

segments.en: Can you help me write a newspaper ad?
segments.zh: 能帮我写一则报纸广告吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: What are you looking to buy or sell?
segments.zh: 你是想买什么，还是卖什么？

segments.en: Actually, I want to hire someone to help me around the house.
segments.zh: 其实，我想雇个人帮我做家务。

segments.en: Oh, you want to get a maid?
segments.zh: 哦，你想请个女佣？

segments.en: Well, I think it's better if you call her a cleaning lady or domestic help.
segments.zh: 我觉得叫清洁阿姨或家政人员更合适。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what do you want her to do?
segments.zh: 那你想让她做些什么？

segments.en: Well, let's see.
segments.zh: 嗯，我们来看看。

segments.en: I want her to come in three times a week for a couple of hours to clean the kitchen, bathroom, and maybe do some cooking.
segments.zh: 我希望她每周来 3 次，持续几个小时来打扫厨房、浴室，也许可以做一些烹饪。

segments.en: Got it.
segments.zh: 明白了。

segments.en: And how much do you offer per month?
segments.zh: 你准备每月付多少？

segments.en: I would pay her hourly.
segments.zh: 我打算按小时付钱。

segments.en: I don't know what the going rate is, though.
segments.zh: 不过，我不知道现在的价格是多少。

segments.en: I know for sure it's more than minimum wage, but maybe you should just negotiate with the person that answers the ad.
segments.zh: 时薪肯定高于最低工资，不过你最好跟应聘的人当面谈谈价。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: I'll be happy to help.
segments.zh: 我很乐意提供帮助。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So talking about minimum wage, is there any exception to why a person would earn less than minimum wage?
segments.zh: 那么说到最低工资，一个人的收入为什么低于最低工资有什么例外吗？

segments.en: I don't believe so.
segments.zh: 我不相信。

segments.en: Well, if they're not legally employed, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，如果他们没有合法就业，对吧？

segments.en: So if you're talking about people who we say are under the table, working under the table, that means that they're not working legally.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您说的是我们说在桌子底下工作的人，这意味着他们没有合法地工作。

segments.en: They're not paying taxes.
segments.zh: 他们不纳税。

segments.en: Then maybe those people will be paid less.
segments.zh: 那么也许这些人的报酬会更少。

segments.en: What about waiters and waitresses?
segments.zh: 服务员和女服务员呢？

segments.en: I've heard that they earn less than minimum wage, but because they earn tips.
segments.zh: 我听说他们的收入低于最低工资，但因为他们赚了小费。

segments.en: This is true.
segments.zh: 这是真的。

segments.en: So most restaurants say, okay, we will pay you as a waiter $3 an hour, but because you will earn tips, you will earn more than the minimum wage.
segments.zh: 所以大多数餐厅都说，好吧，我们会以服务员的身份支付给你每小时 3 美元的费用，但因为你会赚取小费，你的收入将超过最低工资。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this is a good exception.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的例外。

segments.en: Unfortunately, there's no promise.
segments.zh: 不幸的是，没有承诺。

segments.en: If you have no customers, you earn no tips, so you're still earning less than minimum wage.
segments.zh: 如果您没有客户，您没有任何小费，因此您的收入仍然低于最低工资。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But if you have many, many customers and you earn lots of tips and you make $15 an hour or something much higher than the minimum wage.
segments.zh: 但是，如果您有很多很多客户，并且您获得了很多小费，并且您每小时赚 15 美元或远高于最低工资。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And actually being a waiter or a waitress is a very common job that a lot of people have when they're still in school or over the summer.
segments.zh: 实际上，当服务员或女服务员是很多人在上学或暑假时的一项非常常见的工作。

segments.en: And I've heard that it could be quite good because Americans are pretty good tippers.
segments.zh: 我听说这可能非常好，因为美国人是相当不错的小费。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Americans generally tip between 15 and 20%.
segments.zh: 美国人通常在 15% 到 20% 之间小费。

segments.en: And you know that you have to tip because your waiter does not earn a minimum wage.
segments.zh: 而且你知道你必须小费，因为你的服务员没有赚取最低工资。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And so I think there is this expectation.
segments.zh: 所以我认为有这个期望。

segments.en: So if your bill comes out to like a hundred bucks, then you are most definitely going to leave at least a $20 tip.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您的账单达到一百美元，那么您肯定会留下至少 20 美元的小费。

segments.en: Usually, yeah, 15 to $20, $20 if it's that much money.
segments.zh: 通常，是的，如果有那么多钱，15 到 20 美元，20 美元。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: That's very, very interesting, especially considering that in many countries, tipping is not really considered, it's not expected or it's not really something that people do.
segments.zh: 这非常非常有趣，特别是考虑到在许多国家，没有真正考虑小费，这是意料之外的，或者这不是人们真正做的事情。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And in America, it is something that you have to do.
segments.zh: 在美国，这是你必须做的事情。

segments.en: So I think a lot of times when people come to America, they don't expect to pay this.
segments.zh: 所以我想很多时候，当人们来到美国时，他们并不期望支付这笔费用。

segments.en: There's tax, there's tip.
segments.zh: 有税，有小费。

segments.en: So when you see a menu, remember that the cost is a lot higher than you see.
segments.zh: 因此，当您看到菜单时，请记住，成本比您看到的要高得多。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very, very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 非常非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: Let us know if you have any questions, any doubts or comments.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题、任何疑问或意见，请告诉我们。

segments.zh: 您可以在 englishpod.com 找到我们。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
